(service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state transitions).\n\n**PR Checklist (required before merge)**\n- **Tests**: Add/adjust tests covering the new behaviour.\n- **Security**: Update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and add group/record-rule Show me the patch with files changed.\"\n- **Create a wizard**: \"Create a `round_robin_wizard` that generates matches for a stage; include wizard model, view, manifest update, and a unit test verifying match count for 4 teams.\"\n- **Fix workflow behaviour**: \"Investigate why standings recompute includes contested results; propose a minimal fix and tests to prevent contested results from being counted.\"\n\n**Notes & Expectations**\n- **Authoritative sources**: the `_workflows` documents and `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` are the source of truth for business behaviour—use them before changing workflows.\n- **Keep modules decoupled**: the architecture intentionally separates `base`, `tournament`, and the `competition_engine` service; prefer adding features in the appropriate module.\n- **Ask clarifying questions**: if a requested feature impacts tournament rules, scheduling, or publication flows, ask which workflow (`_workflows/*.md`) should govern the behaviour.\n\n**Documentation Maintenance (required)**\n\n- **Always update docs**: For any code, data model, view, workflow, or behaviour change, update the relevant documentation files in this repository as part of the same change set (or in a linked follow-up PR). + {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

`_logs/INSTALL_LOG_*.md`.\n\nCore modules (quick)\n\n- `sports_federation_base`: Master data — clubs, teams, seasons, registrations, base security groups.\n- `sports_federation_tournament`: `sports_federation_calendar`, `sports_federation_scheduling`, `sports_federation_schedule_approval`, and `sports_federation_matchday`: role-owned competition setup, format, capacity, scheduling, publication, and live operations.\n- `sports_federation_people`: Player master data and licensing.\n- `sports_federation_rosters`: Season rosters and match-sheet management.\n- `sports_federation_officiating`: Referee registry and assignments.\n- `sports_federation_result_control`: Result submit/verify/approve pipeline and contest/correction flows.\n- `sports_federation_standings`: Standings computation and publishing.\n- `sports_federation_public_site` / `sports_federation_portal`: Website and portal controllers/templates.\n- `sports_federation_demo`: Deterministic demo records for onboarding walkthroughs and QA sandboxes.\n\nKey workflows (at-a-glance)\n\n- Tournament lifecycle — competition setup, participant enrolment, stage progression, schedule generation, completion. See `odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md`.\n- Match-day operations — roster checks, referee confirmation, match execution, incident logging. See `odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_MATCH_DAY_OPERATIONS.md`.\n- Result pipeline — submit → verify → approve (with contested/corrected exceptions). See `odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_RESULT_PIPELINE.md`.\n- Public publication — `website_published` toggles, public slugs, and safe public pages for tournaments and standings. See `odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_PUBLIC_PUBLICATION.md`.\n\nDeveloper quick-start (most common tasks)\n\n1. Add models: `odoo/<module>/models/<file>.py` and export in `models/__init__.py`.\n2. Security: add `security/ir.model.access.csv` and `security/*.xml` record rules.\n3. Views: add `views/*.xml` and register in `__manifest__.py` `data`.\n4. Wizards/services: put transient models in `wizards/` and algorithmic code in the owning module's `services/` package.\n5. + {"content": "# Integration Contracts\n\nLast updated: 2026-08-20\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document defines the stable partner-facing contracts currently supported by\nthe federation platform and the policy used to version, evolve, and deprecate\nthem.\n\nMachine-readable partner route definitions live in `openapi/integration_v1.yaml`.\nKeep the OpenAPI file, this document, and the route implementations aligned in\nthe same change set whenever a managed integration contract changes.\n\n## Contract Principles\n\n- Every external export or feed must expose an explicit contract identifier.\n- Version changes must be additive within a version whenever possible.\n- Breaking schema changes require a new contract version rather than silent\n  mutation of an existing response.\n- Deprecated routes or payloads remain available for at least one supported\n  release cycle after the replacement contract is published, unless security or\n  legal requirements force a faster removal.\n- Contract changes must be reflected in code, tests where applicable, this\n  document, and the roadmap or release notes in the same change set.\n\n## Authentication Strategy\n\nPublic tournament contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"`\n- intended for website visitors, public calendars, and read-only partner\n  consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner contract subscriptions before a payload is served or a\n  delivery is accepted\n- intended for explicit machine-to-machine integrations without sharing backend\n  user sessions\n\nImport contracts:\n\n- executed either through backend import wizards or through managed partner\n  delivery staging before entering the same wizard flow\n- guarded by dry-run preview, governance-job approval, and checksum matching for\n  live imports\n\n## Public Contracts\n\n## Tournament Feed\n\n- Canonical route: `/api/v1/tournaments/<slug>/feed`\n- Compatibility routes:\n  - `/api/v1/tournaments/<id>/feed`\n  - `/api/v1/competitions/<id>/feed`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_feed`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are allowed in v1 when they do not alter existing\n    semantics\n\n## Tournament Schedule Calendar\n\n- Canonical route: `/tournaments/<slug>/schedule.ics`\n- Compatibility route: `/tournament/<id>/schedule.ics`\n- Response type: `text/calendar`\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: tournament_schedule_ics`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: ics_v1`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n## Authenticated CSV Contracts\n\nAll authenticated CSV exports expose these headers:\n\n- `X-Federation-Contract`\n- `X-Federation-Contract-Version`\n\n## Standings Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/standings/<tournament_id>`\n- Contract: `standings_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n- Notes:\n  - intended for downstream standings review and board-pack style extracts\n\n## Participation Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/participation/<season_id>`\n- Contract: `participation_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Summary Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance`\n- Contract: `finance_summary_csv`\n- Version: `csv_v1`\n\n## Finance Event Handoff Export\n\n- Route: `/reporting/export/finance/events`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Versioning anchor:\n  - detailed finance-event handoff rows expose a schema version column and the\n    matching response header contract version\n- Required handoff fields include:\n  - event identity and state\n  - handoff state\n  - fee type and amount\n  - invoice, external, accounting-batch, and reconciliation references\n  - source traceability\n  - exported, reconciled, and closed timestamps\n\n## Managed Partner Contracts\n\n## Contract Manifest\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/contracts`\n- Response type: `application/json`\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- Payload includes:\n  - contract code, version, direction, transport, and route hint\n  - deprecation stage and replacement contract\n  - `available` flag for database-specific operational availability\n  - partner subscription state and last-used timestamp\n\n## Partner Finance Event Handoff\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/outbound/finance/events`\n- Response type: `text/csv`\n- Contract: `finance_event_v1`\n- Optional query parameters:\n  - `limit` to request one bounded page of rows; defaults to `200` and caps at `500`\n  - `cursor` to resume after the last row from the previous page\n- Invalid `limit` or `cursor` values return `400` with the standard `data_validation` payload.\n- Headers:\n  - `X-Federation-Contract: finance_event_v1`\n  - `X-Federation-Contract-Version: <schema version>`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code: <partner code>`\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Mode: cursor_page` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Export-Count: <row count>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Has-More: true|false` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Page-Limit: <effective limit>` when cursor pagination is active\n  - `X-Federation-Next-Cursor: <timestamp>|<id>` when another page is available\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n\n## Inbound Delivery Staging\n\n- Route: `/integration/v1/inbound/<contract_code>/deliveries`\n- Method: `POST`\n- Request type: JSON object\n- Authentication:\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Code`\n  - `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n  - optional `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key` to safely reuse the same staged delivery for matching retries\n- Request fields:\n  - `filename`\n  - `payload_base64`\n  - optional `notes`\n  - optional `source_reference`\n- Response header on every successful delivery request:\n  - `X-Federation-Delivery-Outcome: created|checksum_reuse|idempotency_replay`\n- Response headers when an idempotency key is supplied:\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotency-Key: <normalized key>`\n  - `X-Federation-Idempotent-Replay: true|false`\n- Response fields:\n  - `delivery_outcome` with `created`, `checksum_reuse`, or `idempotency_replay`\n  - delivery identity and current state\n  - partner and contract codes\n  - echoed `idempotency_key` when present\n  - payload checksum\n  - contract route hint\n- Duplicate handling:\n  - the same partner, contract, and payload checksum reuse the active staged\n    delivery while it remains in preview or approval flow and report\n    `delivery_outcome = checksum_reuse`\n  - the same partner, contract, and idempotency key replay the original delivery\n    across all states, report `delivery_outcome = idempotency_replay`, and\n    still return `400` if the key is reused for a different payload\n\n## Import Contracts\n\nReusable import templates are versioned backend contracts and live under\n`federation.import.template`.\n\nCurrent template codes:\n\n- `clubs_csv`\n- `players_csv`\n- `seasons_csv`\n- `teams_csv`\n- `tournament_participants_csv`\n\nCurrent template version:\n\n- `csv_v1`\n\nManaged inbound delivery policy:\n\n1. A subscribed partner posts a base64 payload to the inbound delivery route for\n  the relevant contract.\n2. The system stages a `federation.integration.delivery` record, deduplicates\n  active resubmissions by checksum, and can also bind an explicit idempotency\n  key to the request for safer client retries.\n3. Operators open the staged delivery in the matching import wizard for preview.\n4. Approval and live execution continue through the standard governance-job\n  workflow already used for manual rollover imports.\n\nLive import policy:\n\n1. Run a dry-run preview for the uploaded CSV.\n2. Request approval, which creates a governance job tied to the file checksum,\n   target model, template, and preview results.\n3. Approve the governance job.\n4. Execute the live import only if the CSV checksum and selected template still\n   match the approved job.\n\nVerification policy:\n\n- governance jobs store preview totals, execution totals, and before/after\n  target-model record counts\n- live imports that partially succeed remain visible as\n  `completed_with_errors`\n- staged partner deliveries mirror preview, approval, completion, and failure\n  states so operators can reconcile inbound handoffs without leaving the app\n\n## Versioning Policy\n\n- Public JSON versions are encoded in both the path and the payload.\n- CSV and ICS contracts use stable routes plus explicit response headers.\n- Import templates use a version field on the template and a matching schema\n  snapshot on the governance job.\n- Breaking changes require a new contract identifier or version rather than a\n  silent replacement.\n\nEndpoint compatibility policy (v1):\n\n- `/integration/v1/contracts`: additive response changes only; To include\nthe demo addon non-interactively, add `--install-demo`.\n\nThe script installs modules that are missing or uninstalled, upgrades modules\nthat are already installed, and restarts the Odoo service. It runs:\n\n- `odoo -c /etc/odoo/odoo.conf -d <db> -i <install_module_csv> -u <upgrade_module_csv> --stop-after-init`\n- `docker compose restart odoo`\n\nThe demo addon is excluded by default. Interactive runs ask whether\n`sports_federation_demo` should be installed. This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, and championship/relegation splits. Dynamic Swiss, ladder, and double-elimination formats are deliberately not advertised as automatic because they require round-by-round or reset-final semantics outside the immutable fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1428, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "7c527aeced8da21ff2fd2701dc53c9ce8e9d1586b33b663b7efda898a87f43dc", "size_bytes": 1428}

This is deliberately\nseparate from the competition engine's `federation.stage.progression` model,\nwhich belongs to tournament-level progression workflows and uses a different\nrelation contract.\n\nBefore generating a structure, the graph is validated for cycles. Root stages\ncan then be prepared; dependent stages wait for incoming progression results.\nApproved fixture results can populate dependent stages, and frozen standings\nare stored as immutable snapshots.\n\nStage-graph access rules are loaded from `security/ir.model.access.csv`. The\nstructure form extension identifies the stage tab by its `stage_ids` field so\nthe view remains safe when translated page labels change.\n## Supported format generation\n\nThe format studio now estimates fixture and round counts before generation. It supports single and double leagues, seeded knockout and placement brackets, match series, pool-to-knockout configuration, championship/relegation splits, Swiss rounds, ladder formats, and power-of-two double elimination. Swiss round counts are configurable on the structure, while double elimination uses the dynamic pairing service to account for its winner, loser, and reset-final routes. These estimates are planning guidance; format-specific generation workflows remain responsible for validating the final fixture graph.\n", "content_length": 1599, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_format/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "a77ea3a8e64ed4bd839025fe8e3e21961d32e160ec3c607bd480eaa5b7eb539d", "size_bytes": 1599}

No\nproduction data migration is required solely for this ownership clarification.\n\n## Capability ownership\n\n- Competition Core owns edition lifecycle and role assignments.\n- Registration owns entries and versioned finalized participant sets.\n- Format Studio owns stage topology, logical fixtures, standings snapshots, and progression.\n- Calendar owns physical match days, courts, and availability slots.\n- Scheduling owns fixture-to-slot assignments and fairness proposals.\n- Schedule Approval owns independent review and immutable publications.\n- Result Control owns the complete result lifecycle.\n- Match-Day Operations owns live execution and incidents.\n\n## Domain event contract\n\nEvents are past-tense facts. - {"content": "# Sports Federation Governance\n\nFormal override-request workflow with decisions and audit trails. Provides a\nstructured way for federation officials to request, review, and implement\nexceptions to standard processes.\n\n## Purpose\n\nSome situations require bending the rules — late registrations, replayed matches,\nexceptional eligibility grants. This module ensures those exceptions are\n**requested, decided, logged, and auditable** rather than happening informally.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n| Module | Reason |\n|--------|--------|\n| `sports_federation_base` | Core entities |\n| `sports_federation_people` | Player references |\n| `sports_federation_tournament` | Tournament references |\n| `mail` | Chatter |\n\n## Models\n\n### `federation.override.request`\n\nA formal request to override a standard process.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `name` | Char | Request title |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Type of override |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Linked record |\n| `requested_by_id` | Many2one | Requester (user) |\n| `requested_on` | Datetime | Request timestamp |\n| `state` | Selection | draft / submitted / approved / rejected / implemented / closed |\n| `reason` | Text | Justification |\n| `implementation_note` | Text | How it was applied |\n| `decision_ids` | One2many | Review decisions |\n| `audit_note_ids` | One2many | Audit trail entries |\n| `outcome_ids` | One2many | Post-decision outcome log |\n\n- **State machine**: draft → submitted → approved / rejected → implemented → closed, with submitted requests withdrawable back to draft before a decision is recorded.\n\n### `federation.override.decision`\n\nA review decision on an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `decision` | Selection | approve / reject / request_info |\n| `decided_by_id` | Many2one | Decision maker |\n| `decided_on` | Datetime | Decision timestamp |\n| `note` | Text | Reasoning |\n\n### `federation.audit.note`\n\nFree-form audit notes attached to an override request.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | The request |\n| `note` | Text | Audit remark |\n| `author_id` | Many2one | Author |\n| `created_on` | Datetime | Timestamp |\n\n### `federation.override.outcome`\n\nOutcome tracking row attached to an override request after implementation or\nfollow-up review.\n\n| Field | Type | Description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| `request_id` | Many2one | Source override request |\n| `outcome` | Selection | implemented / effective / partial / ineffective / reversed |\n| `outcome_on` | Datetime | When the outcome was recorded |\n| `recorded_by_id` | Many2one | Operator recording the outcome |\n| `request_type` | Selection | Snapshot of the originating request type |\n| `target_model` / `target_res_id` | Char / Integer | Snapshot of the overridden record |\n| `request_state` | Selection | Request state at the time of logging |\n| `note` | Text | Outcome commentary |\n\n## Security Groups\n\n| Group | Purpose |\n|-------|---------|\n| Governance Officer | Can review and decide on override requests |\n\n## Key Behaviours\n\n1. **Formal request lifecycle** — Every exception starts as a draft request,\n   can be withdrawn back to draft while still submitted, and otherwise follows\n   a structured approval flow.\n2. **Multi-decision support** — Multiple governance officers can weigh in on a\n   single request.\n3. **Audit trail** — All decisions and notes are timestamped and attributed.\n4. **Generic target** — Requests can link to any record type via model/res_id.\n5. **Outcome evidence** — implemented requests now create outcome-log rows so\n   governance review can extend beyond the approval moment.\n", "content_length": 3754,   {"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. Bootstrap confirmation dialogs move\nfocus into the dialog and restore it to the invoking control when closed.\nKeyboard focus uses a visible outline that does not depend on color-only status\ncues. The focused accessibility suite covers these contracts together with\nmobile table and action wrapping.\n", "content_length": 3540, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3ea4f6e8c7c0686f04a9a5a78e3b76b66861847771f9655441258519bd4016a5", "size_bytes": 3540}

+-{"content": "Sports Federation Standings\n===========================\n\nComputes and stores league-style standings tables for tournament stages and\ngroups. Aggregates match results into a ranked table with points, wins,\nlosses, goal differences, and configurable tie-break ordering.\n\nPurpose\n-------\n\nProvides a snapshot of competition standings that can be published, audited,\nand used by downstream modules such as the public site, reporting, and\nqualification logic. Standings are linked to rule sets to ensure consistent\nscoring and tie resolution.\n\nDependencies\n------------\n\n- ``sports_federation_tournament``: Tournaments, stages, groups, and matches.\n- ``sports_federation_rules``: Rule sets for scoring and tie-breaks.\n- ``mail``: Chatter integration.\n\nModels\n------\n\n``federation.standing``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nA standings table for a specific scope such as a tournament, stage, or group.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``name`` (Char): Standings title.\n- ``tournament_id`` (Many2one): Tournament.\n- ``stage_id`` (Many2one): Optional stage scope.\n- ``group_id`` (Many2one): Optional group scope.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Competition context.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Scoring and tie-break rules.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``computed``, or ``frozen``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Ranked team entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``computed_on`` (Datetime): When the table was last computed.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Additional notes.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> computed -> frozen``.\n\n``federation.standing.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nOne row per participant in the standings table.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Parent standings.\n- ``participant_id`` (Many2one): The team.\n- ``rank`` (Integer): Position in the standings table (1 = first).\n- ``played`` (Integer): Total matches played.\n- ``won`` / ``drawn`` / ``lost`` (Integer): Results breakdown.\n- ``score_for`` / ``score_against`` (Integer): Goals/points scored and conceded.\n- ``score_diff`` (Integer, computed): ``score_for - score_against``.\n- ``points`` (Integer): Total points per rule set.\n- ``note`` (Char): Short free-text remark for this line.\n- ``tiebreak_notes`` (Text, readonly): Auto-generated explanation of the tie-break criterion used to order this participant.\n\n``federation.standing.recompute.job``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAsynchronous recompute queue record used for background standings updates.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Target standing to recompute.\n- ``idempotency_key`` (Char): Replay-safe key for deduplicating repeated queue requests.\n- ``correlation_id`` (Char): Trace identifier propagated through queue processing.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``pending``, ``running``, ``done``, or ``failed``.\n- ``attempt_count`` / ``max_attempts`` (Integer): Retry control metadata.\n- ``requested_on`` / ``started_on`` / ``completed_on`` (Datetime): Lifecycle timestamps.\n- ``next_retry_on`` (Datetime): Retry schedule for failed jobs.\n- ``last_error`` (Text): Last failure reason captured for operators.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Rule-set driven scoring**: points are calculated using the attached rule\n   set and its configured win, draw, and loss values.\n- **Tie-break resolution**: when teams have equal points, tie-break rules from\n   the rule set are applied in sequence order.\n- **Snapshot model**: each standings record is a point-in-time computation,\n   allowing historical comparison.\n- **Official-result filtering**: when ``sports_federation_result_control`` is\n   installed, only matches with ``include_in_official_standings = True`` are\n   counted.\n- **Freeze behavior**: frozen standings reject recomputation unless\n   ``force_recompute`` is provided in context.\n- **Auto-advance hook**: freezing a standing can trigger pending\n   ``federation.stage.progression`` rules with ``auto_advance = True``.\n- **Publication is separate**: public visibility is handled by\n   ``sports_federation_public_site`` through ``website_published``, not by a\n   dedicated published standings state.\n- **Optional queued recompute**: standings can be recomputed asynchronously via\n   ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` and the\n   ``action_queue_recompute`` button.\n- **Idempotent queue requests**: repeated queue requests with the same\n   ``idempotency_key`` replay the original job instead of creating duplicates.\n- **Queue visibility**: pending and failed queue counters are surfaced directly\n   on the standing form, with a dedicated queue action and menu entry.\n\n## Migration note (v19.0.1.2.0)\n\n- Adds ``federation.standing.recompute.job`` for asynchronous, idempotent\n   standings recompute processing.\n- Adds queue cron ``Standings: Process Recompute Queue``.\n\n## Recompute job recovery\n\nStanding recompute jobs use bounded exponential retry. Exhausted jobs move to `Needs operator action`, preserve the correlation ID and error evidence, and can be explicitly returned to the queue by a manager. The queue cron also recovers jobs left in `running` after a worker interruption.\n", "content_length": 5027, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_standings/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "fac9e6593f4665d79b936eb12082894d8ee14db0fedb13c468f646ae81dda197", "size_bytes": 5027}

 {"content": "**Repository Summary**\n- **Purpose**: Odoo 19 custom addons to manage a sports federation (clubs, teams, seasons, tournaments, rules, officiating, rosters, results, public site, reporting).\n- **Location**: All addons live under the `odoo/` folder as individual modules prefixed with `sports_federation_`.\n-- **Primary docs**: See [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1), [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1), and the Workflows in [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1).\n\n**Architecture & Patterns**\n- **Module split**: `sports_federation_base` (master data), `sports_federation_tournament` (tournaments, matches, participants), `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (service/wizards), plus domain modules (`people`, `rules`, `officiating`, `rosters`, `result_control`, `public_site`, `reporting`, `finance_bridge`, `venues`, `discipline`, `standings`, ...).\n- **Model naming**: Domain models use the `federation.` prefix (e.g. `federation.player`, `federation.match`).\n- **Common patterns**: `ir.sequence` for identifiers, `state` selection fields for workflows, wizards for batch operations (under `wizards/`), `controllers/` for portal/website endpoints, and `security/` for groups/record rules/ACLs.\n\n**Key Files & Where To Look**\n- **High-level context**: [odoo/CONTEXT.md](odoo/CONTEXT.md#L1)\n- **Technical architecture**: [odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md](odoo/TECHNICAL_NOTE.md#L1)\n-- **Workflows (authoritative behavioural spec)**: [odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md](odoo/_workflows/WORKFLOW_TOURNAMENT_LIFECYCLE.md#L1) and the other files inside `odoo/_workflows`.\n- **Module READMEs**: each module may have a `README.md` under `odoo/<module>/README.md` with implementation notes and expectations.\n-- **Install logs / historical notes**: `_logs/` contains installation and setup notes per module.\n\n**Development Guidelines (how to implement changes)**\n- **Add/modify a model**: create/modify `models/*.py`, export package in `models/__init__.py`, add access rules in `security/ir.model.access.csv`, add any initial `data/*.xml` and register them in `__manifest__.py` `data` or `demo` lists, add views in `views/*.xml`, update `menu_items.xml` as needed, and add tests under `tests/`.\n- **Add a wizard or service**: put transient models under `wizards/` and views under `views/` (manifest `data`), keep service logic in modules like `sports_federation_format / sports_federation_scheduling` (no persistent models if not required).\n- **Add a controller / portal flow**: use `controllers/` and add templates under `views/` or `templates/`; respect portal record rules (see `sports_federation_portal`).\n- **Security**: always add or update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and any `security/*.xml` groups/rules for new models or new endpoints.\n- **Manifest hygiene**: update `__manifest__.py` `depends`, `data`, and `version` fields when introducing DB changes or new data files.\n\n**Testing & Local Run**\n- **Where tests live**: `odoo/<module>/tests/` when present (some modules include unit/functional tests).\n- **Run module tests**: use the Odoo test runner for module-level tests (e.g. `odoo-bin -d <db> -i <module> --test-enable`) or your established local development workflow.\n- **Release sanity**: include at least one focused test for new business logic (especially schedule generation, result pipeline, and state transitions).\n\n**PR Checklist (required before merge)**\n- **Tests**: Add/adjust tests covering the new behaviour.\n- **Security**: Update `security/ir.model.access.csv` and add group/record-rule XML if necessary.\n- **Manifest**: Add new data files to `__manifest__.py` `data` list and ensure `depends` are correct.\n-- **Docs**: Update or add a short README in the module and, if behaviour changes, update the relevant `odoo/_workflows` file.\n- **Small, focused commits**: Prefer atomic commits (one logical change per commit) and descriptive commit messages.\n\n**How Copilot Should Help (recommended prompts & behaviour)**\n- **Primary rule**: Prefer conservative, minimal changes that keep module boundaries intact. Avoid touching unrelated modules unless absolutely required and explain why.\n- **When asked to implement a model change**: return a plan and a single patch that includes: the `models/<file>.py` change, `models/__init__.py` export, `security/ir.model.access.csv` entry, `views/*.xml` (if UI), `__manifest__.py` update, and a new test under `tests/` that exercises the main logic.\n- **When asked to add a wizard or generator**: create a transient model in `wizards/`, a wizard view, and a small deterministic example in tests that demonstrates expected output (e.g. round-robin schedule for 4 participants).\n- **When asked about business rules or workflows**: consult and reference the Workflow docs in `odoo/_workflows` and the `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` to ensure behaviour matches the documented flows.\n\n**Example prompts you can give Copilot in this repo**\n- **Add a model**: \"Add a new persistent model `federation.referee` with fields `name`, `certification_level`, `active`; add ACLs, a basic tree/form view, and unit tests. Show me the patch with files changed.\"\n- **Create a wizard**: \"Create a `round_robin_wizard` that generates matches for a stage; include wizard model, view, manifest update, and a unit test verifying match count for 4 teams.\"\n- **Fix workflow behaviour**: \"Investigate why standings recompute includes contested results; propose a minimal fix and tests to prevent contested results from being counted.\"\n\n**Notes & Expectations**\n- **Authoritative sources**: the `_workflows` documents and `TECHNICAL_NOTE.md` are the source of truth for business behaviour—use them before changing workflows.\n- **Keep modules decoupled**: the architecture intentionally separates `base`, `tournament`, and the `competition_engine` service; prefer adding features in the appropriate module.\n- **Ask clarifying questions**: if a requested feature impacts tournament rules, scheduling, or publication flows, ask which workflow (`_workflows/*.md`) should govern the behaviour.\n\n**Documentation Maintenance (required)**\n\n- **Always update docs**: For any code, data model, view, workflow, or behaviour change, update the relevant documentation files in this repository as part of the same change set (or in a linked follow-up PR).  {"content": "# Competition Engine\n\nThis implementation provides role-owned capabilities and explicit handovers for competition planning and operations.\n\n## Addons\n\n1. `sports_federation_competition_core`: identity, roles, lifecycle and events.\n2. `sports_federation_registration`: application queue and finalized participant sets.\n3. `sports_federation_format`: versioned logical structures and fixtures.\n4. `sports_federation_calendar`: physical match days, round allocations and capacity.\n5. `sports_federation_scheduling`: one-way fixture-to-slot assignments, pure validation and deterministic proposals.\n6. `sports_federation_schedule_approval`: independent review and immutable publication snapshots.\n7. `sports_federation_matchday`: live operational control and incidents.\n\n## Required handovers\n\nRegistration finalizes a participant set. Format freezes a structure. Calendar prepares physical capacity. Scheduling submits a complete schedule. Approval publishes an immutable snapshot. Match-day operations execute only a published snapshot.\n\n## Migration policy\n\nThe legacy monolithic engine has been removed from the addon set. New and existing operational flows use the ownership split. Databases upgraded from a release that installed the legacy addon require the normal reviewed upgrade/migration procedure before production rollout; do not silently reinterpret existing production records.\n\n\n## Schedule handoff operator handoff\n\nThe operator path is fully exposed in the backend: Schedule Planner submits a\nvalidated revision, Schedule Review Queue provides independent request-changes\nor approval decisions, Publication exposes approved schedules and immutable\npublication history, and Match-Day Operations consumes only the current live\npublication. Submission creates its pending review atomically when the approval\naddon is installed; there is no operator-visible intermediate state that\nrequires a separate \"start review\" action.\n\n## Phases 5.1.1 to 5.3: publication and live operations\n\nSchedule review decisions are command-only: ACLs are read-only and the review\nmodel rejects direct decision-field writes. Live publications are scoped and\nversioned per match day. Publication replacement uses a dedicated wizard,\nrequires a replacement reason, locks the match day during version allocation,\nand rejects stale confirmations.\n\nMatch-Day Control exposes readiness, the exact live publication, published\nmatches, court state, incidents, immutable sessions and operational deviations.\nOpening a day freezes the publication digest in a session. Live moves, delays,\npostponements and cancellations update only operational match fields; the\napproved publication and `published_slot_id` remain immutable. Every deviation\nrecords actor, reason, old/new slot, session and publication, and emits an audit\nevent.\n", "content_length": 2809, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "COMPETITION_ENGINE.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "2c6a2ef0be5e1aece6060a09b33b5da37b58fc1a0bca7e3604aa9cde951df0b0", "size_bytes": 2809}

 {"content": "# Contributing\n\nThis repository expects small, test-backed changes with matching documentation updates.\n\n## Prerequisites\n\n- Python 3.10 or newer for local linting\n- Docker with Compose current for the containerized Odoo test runner\n- Git Bash, WSL, or another POSIX shell for the `ci/*.sh` scripts on Windows\n\n## Local setup\n\n```bash\ncp ci/.env.example ci/.env\npython -m pip install --upgrade pip\npython -m pip install -r requirements.txt\n```\n\nKeep `ci/.env` local-only. Integration keys can be copied from `ci/integrations.env.example` or provided by your shell environment.\n\n## Focused test commands\n\nRun targeted suites for the main maintained flows:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite portal_public_ops\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite finance_reporting\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite rosters_readiness_guard\n```\n\nRun an individual module when you only need a narrow slice:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_result_control\n```\n\nList the named suites from the runner itself:\n\n```bash\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n## Pre-push checks\n\nBefore release qualification, commit or intentionally discard all tracked\nchanges and remove generated runtime configuration. The RC preflight enforces\nthat the candidate can be reproduced from its commit:\n\n```bash\nscripts/ci/run_rc_validation.sh preflight\n```\n\nRun the normal development checks afterward:\n\n```bash\nblack --check sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nflake8 sports_federation_base sports_federation_tournament sports_federation_standings sports_federation_venues sports_federation_portal sports_federation_public_site ci\nbash -n ci/run_tests.sh\nbash -n ci/apply_env_to_ir_config.sh\nbash -n ci/restore_backup_drill.sh\npython3 ci/check_doc_freshness.py\npython3 ci/check_markdown_links.py\npython3 ci/check_module_owners.py\npython3 ci/check_openapi_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_release_train.py\npython3 ci/check_explain_snapshots.py\npython3 ci/check_ci_hygiene.py\npython3 ci/check_workflow_state_contracts.py\npython3 ci/check_module_dependency_drift.py\nbash ci/prune_ci_logs.sh 30\n```\n\n## CI/CD Pipeline\n\n### Named test suites\n\nThe CI runner groups modules into named suites for focused feedback. Use the\nsuite that covers the area you changed:\n\n| Suite | Modules covered |\n|---|---|\n| `competition_core` | Base, tournament, scheduling, results, standings critical path |\n| `portal_public_ops` | Portal ownership, public routes, compliance, standings, venue-facing flows |\n| `finance_reporting` | Finance bridge and reporting coverage |\n| `rosters_readiness_guard` | Participant readiness regression and discovery gate |\n| `release_surfaces` | Broader portal/public, match-day, compliance, notification release verification |\n| `people_rosters_rules` | People, rosters, rules, and officiating modules |\n| `ops_and_notifications` | Discipline, governance, notifications, import_tools, demo modules |\n\n```bash\n# Run a named suite\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --suite competition_core\n\n# Run a single module (fastest for narrow changes)\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_standings\n\n# Run everything (use before merging)\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh\n\n# List suites\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --list-suites\n```\n\n### Reading CI output\n\nThe runner prints a results block at the end:\n\n```\n════════════════════════════════\n  RESULTS\n════════════════════════════════\n  Exit code:     0\n  Tests run:     62\n  Tests passed:  62\n  Tests failed:  0\n  Test errors:   0\n════════════════════════════════\n```\n\nA non-zero exit code means failure. Find the cause:\n\n```bash\n# Show failing test names and tracebacks\ndocker logs <container> 2>&1 | grep -A 20 \"FAIL\\|ERROR\\|Traceback\"\n```\n\nThe container name is printed by `docker compose ps` or appears in the runner\noutput as `sf_ci-ci-odoo-run-<hash>`.\n\n### CI gate stages\n\n1. **Module install** — all declared modules install without error.\n2. **Test run** — `TransactionCase` and `HttpCase` tests execute.\n3. **Query-count checks** — `assertQueryCount` assertions verify no N+1\n   regressions were introduced.\n4. **EXPLAIN snapshots** — `ci/check_explain_snapshots.py` compares query\n   plans against stored baselines.\n5. **Doc freshness checks** — `ci/check_doc_freshness.py`, `check_markdown_links.py`,\n   `check_module_owners.py`, `check_openapi_contracts.py` verify documentation\n   and contracts are up to date.\n6. **Workflow contract checks** — `ci/check_workflow_state_contracts.py` verifies\n   that documented lifecycle states and required workflow actions stay aligned\n   with model declarations.\n\n### Workflow contract map upkeep\n\n- Keep `_workflows/contracts/workflow_state_contracts.json` aligned with each\n  canonical workflow markdown and model state source.\n- If CI reports undocumented states, either add the state to the matching\n  workflow markdown and contract entry or remove/rename the code state.\n- If CI reports missing actions, add the action method in code with the\n  expected guardrails or update the contract when the workflow changed by design.\n\n### Iterating on a failing test\n\n```bash\n# 1. Make your code change\n# 2. Run only the affected module\nbash ./ci/run_tests.sh --module sports_federation_<name>\n# 3. consumption\n\nOperator-authenticated reporting exports:\n\n- `auth=\"user\"`\n- require an authenticated backend session\n- intended for federation operators using backend actions and reporting screens\n\nManaged partner contracts:\n\n- `auth=\"public\"` routes protected by partner credentials\n- require `X-Federation-Partner-Code` and `X-Federation-Partner-Token`\n- enforce per-partner `X-Federation-Contract-Version: v1`\n- Payload anchor:\n  - top-level `api_version = \"v1\"`\n- Stability expectation:\n  - top-level keys in the v1 payload are stable\n  - additive nested fields are expectation:\n  - calendar structure stays compatible with standard ICS consumers\n  - field enrichment should be additive inside event descriptions, not a change\n    to the ICS envelope\n\n##  {"content": "# State And Ownership Matrix\n\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-05-20\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nThis document records the canonical lifecycle states and ownership boundaries\nfor the federation records called out in the roadmap. It is intended to keep\ncontrollers, record rules, tests, and workflow docs aligned with the code.\n\n## Canonical records\n\n| Record | Module | Primary owner | Create path | Canonical states | Ownership boundary | Notes |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| `federation.tournament` | `sports_federation_tournament` + `sports_federation_portal` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, scheduling services, website publication helpers | `draft`, `open`, `in_progress`, `closed`, `cancelled` | Federation-owned season / competition scope | Portal tournament workspaces only expose active tournaments (`open`, `in_progress`) and only for teams inside the user's current whole-club or explicit team scope. |\n| `federation.match` | `sports_federation_tournament` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, scheduling services, wizards | `draft`, `scheduled`, `in_progress`, `done`, `cancelled` | Federation-owned tournament/stage/group | Official standings inclusion is further gated by `include_in_official_standings` when `sports_federation_result_control` is installed. |\n| `federation.schedule.slot` | `sports_federation_calendar` | Calendar operations prepare capacity; scheduling assigns fixtures; approval publishes the resulting schedule | Match-day calendar and scheduling views | `available`, `break`, `blocked` | Federation-owned match day / playing-area scope | A slot belongs to one match day. Fixture assignment and overlap validation are enforced server-side. |\n| `federation.standing` | `sports_federation_standings` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI, recompute/freeze actions | `draft`, `computed`, `frozen` | Federation-owned tournament/stage/group | Only computed or frozen standings are publication candidates. |\n| `federation.tournament.participant` | `sports_federation_tournament` | Federation competition operations | Backend UI or confirmed tournament registration | `registered`, `confirmed`, `withdrawn` | Team's club within a federation tournament | Portal users do not write participants directly; confirmed registrations may create them. |\n| `federation.competition.entry` | `sports_federation_portal` | Shared: club representative submits, federation staff reviews | Portal form or backend UI | `draft`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `rejected`, `cancelled` | Team must belong to one of the submitting user's represented clubs | This is the review buffer before participant creation. |\n| `federation.season.registration` | `sports_federation_base` + `sports_federation_portal` | Shared: club representative submits, federation staff confirms | Portal form or backend UI | `draft`, `submitted`, `confirmed`, `cancelled` | Team must belong to one of the submitting user's represented clubs | Portal extension adds `submitted`, `user_id`, and `rejection_reason`. Rejecting a registration returns it to `draft`; there is no persistent `rejected` enum. |\n| `federation.finance.event` | `sports_federation_finance_bridge` | Federation finance operations and approved workflow hooks | Backend UI or workflow automation | `draft`, `confirmed`, `settled`, `cancelled` | Source record remains authoritative; finance staff own settlement/cancellation | Season-registration confirmation and match finance hooks create events automatically. |\n\n## Archive behavior\n\nThe core master-data records now expose explicit archive and restore actions in\nthe backend UI so operational records do not disappear through ad hoc writes to\n`active`.\n\n| Record | Archive guardrail |\n| --- | --- |\n| `federation.club` | Clubs can only be archived after their active teams are archived. |\n| `federation.team` | Teams can only be archived when all linked season registrations are cancelled. |\n| `federation.season` | Open seasons must be closed or cancelled before they can be archived. |\n| `federation.tournament` | Open or in-progress tournaments must be closed or cancelled before they can be archived. |\n\n## Transition ownership\n\n| Record | Transition owners | Guardrails |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| `federation.tournament` | Federation staff for lifecycle transitions; portal layer for read-only workspace access | Portal workspace helpers must revalidate both active-tournament scope and the caller's visible team or club scope before any elevated detail read. |\n| `federation.match` | Federation staff, scheduling services, result-control roles | Public routes are read-only. Match completion may trigger bracket advancement, and result-control transitions may trigger non-frozen standings recomputation. |\n| `federation.schedule.slot` | Calendar owns slot capacity and lifecycle; scheduling assigns fixtures; schedule approval publishes the resulting schedule | Slot availability and capacity are prepared by `sports_federation_calendar`; assignment validation is enforced by `sports_federation_scheduling`; approved schedules are immutable and published by `sports_federation_schedule_approval`. |\n| `federation.standing` | Federation staff | Frozen standings block recomputation unless forced. |\n| `federation.tournament.participant` | Federation staff, confirmed registration flow | Tournament/team eligibility is validated on create and update. |\n| `federation.competition.entry` | Portal club representatives for submission/cancel, federation staff for confirm/reject | Controllers validate club ownership and the model enforces ownership as defense in depth. |\n| `federation.season.registration` | Portal club representatives for submission/cancel, federation staff for confirm | Controllers validate club ownership and the model must enforce ownership as defense in depth. |\n| `federation.finance.event` | Federation finance staff for confirm/settle/cancel; approved workflow hooks for draft creation | Auto-created events must stay idempotent per source record and fee type. |\n\n## Enum reconciliation\n\nUse the model enums below in code, docs, and tests:\n\n- Tournament lifecycle ends in `closed`, not `completed`.\n- Match lifecycle ends in `done`, not `completed`.\n- Competition planning is handed over through registration, format freeze, calendar capacity, scheduling, approval publication, and match-day execution.\n- Schedule slots use the calendar lifecycle `available`, `break`, and `blocked`; schedule approval protects published snapshots from routine edits.\n- Tournament registration review uses `submitted` and `rejected`.\n- Season registration review uses `submitted`; there is no `rejected` state in the current model.\n- Finance event lifecycle uses `settled`; `invoiced` and `paid` are future integration concepts, not current model states.\n- Seasons only open from `draft`, close from `open`, and return to `draft` from `cancelled`.\n- Tournaments only open from `draft`, start from `open`, close from `in_progress`, and return to `draft` from `cancelled`.\n\n## Review checklist\n\n- New controller writes must validate represented-club ownership before any `sudo().create()` or state change.\n- Portal tournament workspace reads and match-day record rules must revalidate active-tournament scope plus the user's current `portal_club_scope_ids` and `portal_team_scope_ids` before any elevated read or cross-team search.\n- Portal roster detail, roster-line edit, and roster-line license paths must resolve ids through the shared portal privilege boundary instead of raw elevated browse calls.\n- Public website routes must enforce `website_published` and the relevant visibility toggle before reading data with `sudo()`, and slug or numeric compatibility routes must resolve records through those publication-scoped domains up front.\n- State transitions referenced in docs and workflows must match the real selection values in the models.\n", "content_length": 7935, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "STATE_AND_OWNERSHIP_MATRIX.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "c4dba91069618fea21c73ed5c8c6ac1bdc093b8cdc3f2c9634a6cadcbebd6428", "size_bytes": 7935}

A menu can be hidden if the current user lacks the required role or record access.\n\n## Actual backend menu map\n\n```text\nFederation\n├── Setup\n│   ├── Core Records\n│   │   ├── Clubs\n│   │   └── Teams\n│   ├── Seasons\n│   ├── Season Registrations\n│   └── Competition Setup\n│       ├── Competition Templates\n│       ├── Season Competitions\n│       └── Rules & Policies\n├── Competition Workflow\n│   ├── Create Competition\n│   ├── Competition Overview\n│   ├── Registration Desk\n│   ├── Format Studio\n│   ├── Format Templates\n│   ├── Calendar Planner\n│   ├── Schedule Planner\n│   ├── Schedule Review Queue\n│   ├── Match-Day Control\n│   └── Technical Records\n├── Planning\n│   ├── Operational Action Queue\n│   └── Advanced Records\n│       ├── Divisions & Tournaments\n│       ├── Matches\n│       └── Tournament Structure\n├── Match Day\n│   ├── Match Sheets\n│   ├── Venues\n│   ├── Officiating\n│   └── Discipline\n├── Publication\n│   ├── Standings\n│   ├── Approved Schedules\n│   └── Schedule Publications\n└── Administration\n    ├── Reporting\n    │   └── Operational Health\n    ├── Retention and Recovery\n    ├── Retention Evidence\n    └── Operational Job Health\n```\n\nThere is no backend menu named **Competitions**, **Registrations**, **Scheduling**, **Schedule Approval**, **Results**, or **Competition Engine**. Those are concepts or addon names, not current navigation labels.\n\n## Actual club portal links\n\n```text\nMy Account\n├── Overview                 /my/competitions\n├── Action items             /my/action-items\n├── My teams                 /my/teams\n├── Season registrations     /my/season-registrations\n├── Match day                /my/match-day\n├── Officials                /my/referee-duties\n└── Results                  /my/results\n```\n\n## Complete workflow and recovery\n\n### 1. Prepare reusable setup\n\nUse:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Seasons\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Competition Templates\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Rules & Policies > Rule Sets & Policies\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Clubs\nFederation > Setup > Core Records > Teams\n```\n\nCreate the season, reusable competition definition, rule set, clubs, and teams. Points, tie-break, eligibility, and qualification components are below **Rules & Policies > Advanced Components**.\n\n**Recovery:** Edit unused records. Archive records that already have history. Do not delete referenced seasons, competitions, clubs, teams, or rule sets merely to restart a workflow.\n\n### 2. Create the season competition\n\nPreferred menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Create Competition\n```\n\nThe wizard selects the setup template, competition template, season, dates, optional rule set, registration dates, divisions, and responsibilities. It creates the season competition, divisions, registration windows, and role assignments, then opens the season competition.\n\nInspect the records through:\n\n```text\nFederation > Setup > Competition Setup > Season Competitions\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Divisions & Tournaments\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Competition Overview\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Correct newly created records before clubs submit. There is no generic **Undo Competition Wizard** button. If downstream entries, fixtures, schedules, results, or publications exist, preserve the original records and create controlled replacements.\n\n### 3. Open registration and accept entries\n\nBackend:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Season registrations\n```\n\nUse **Open Registration** on a draft registration window. Clubs prepare and submit entries. Managers review them in the Registration Desk.\n\n**Recovery:** Use **Close Registration** to stop submissions. A submitted entry can be withdrawn by the club or returned by the manager with a reason. A returned entry can be corrected and resubmitted. Rejection remains historical evidence.\n\n### 4. Finalize participants\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Registration Desk\n```\n\nClose the registration window and press **Finalize Participants**. The finalized participant set feeds the format structure.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct entries before finalization. If a finalized set is wrong and nothing depends on it, create a corrected set through the registration workflow. If fixtures or schedules exist, create a successor structure or schedule revision instead of mutating published history.\n\n### 5. Configure and generate the format\n\nMenus:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Templates\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\n**Format Templates** is manager-only. In **Format Studio**, select the season competition, division, finalized participant set, and format settings. Use **Check Feasibility**, then **Generate Fixtures**. For multi-stage structures use **Validate Stage Graph**. Once accepted, use **Freeze Structure**.\n\n**Recovery:** Before freeze, correct and regenerate. Once operational matches or frozen stage snapshots exist, create a new structure version. The current UI has no generic structure-unfreeze command.\n\n### 6. Prepare and progress stages\n\nThere is no standalone **Stage Progression** menu. Stage controls are on the structure opened from:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Format Studio\n```\n\nAvailable stage actions are **Prepare**, **Start**, and **Freeze & Progress**.\n\n**Recovery:** Correct a stage before starting it. Before progression, correct and recompute standings. Frozen snapshot lines are immutable; after progression use a corrected successor structure rather than editing evidence.\n\n### 7. Plan calendar capacity\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Calendar Planner\n```\n\nCreate match days, slot windows, and capacity, then use **Mark Capacity Ready**. Venue setup and constraints are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Venues\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Edit draft calendar records. If a schedule already uses the calendar, make the deliberate calendar correction and refresh the working schedule. Stale assignments are flagged, not silently deleted.\n\n### 8. Build the working schedule\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Refresh Calendar Fixtures**. Assign dates, times, venues, and courts manually, or use **Auto-schedule**, **Preview**, and **Apply Auto-schedule**. Review fairness warnings.\n\n**Recovery:** Draft and change-requested schedules remain editable. A preview does not change the schedule until applied. Refresh fixtures, move assignments, or regenerate while mutable.\n\n### 9. Submit and review the schedule\n\nPlanner menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner\n```\n\nUse **Submit for Review**. Approver menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Review Queue\n```\n\nThe review exposes **Withdraw Submission**, **Request Changes**, and **Approve Schedule** according to state and role.\n\n**Recovery:** Withdraw a pending submission to return it to editing. Request changes to return it to the planner. If an approval is mistaken, do not publish; correct it through a new review cycle while preserving separation of duties.\n\n### 10. Publish the schedule\n\nUse **Publish Schedule** on an approved review. The two real publication menus are:\n\n```text\nFederation > Publication > Approved Schedules\nFederation > Publication > Schedule Publications\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Live publications are immutable. Open the published schedule under **Federation > Competition Workflow > Schedule Planner**, use **Amend Schedule**, enter a reason, and press **Create Amendment**. The replacement follows submit, review, approve, and publish again. The old publication becomes superseded. There is no in-place **Unpublish** button.\n\n### 11. Operate match day\n\nMenu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Match-Day Control\n```\n\nUse **Open Match Day** when ready. During operations use **Update Court**, **Report Incident**, or **Operational Schedule Change**. Finish with **Close Match Day**. Supporting records are under:\n\n```text\nFederation > Match Day > Match Sheets\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Incidents\nFederation > Competition Workflow > Technical Records > Operational Deviations\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Resolve incident and deviation records with **Resolve**. Operational changes are recorded rather than silently altering the approved publication. Correct the planning baseline through a schedule amendment.\n\n### 12. Submit and approve results\n\nBackend menu:\n\n```text\nFederation > Planning > Advanced Records > Matches\n```\n\nResult Control extends the match form; there is no separate backend **Results** menu. The form provides **Submit Result**, **Verify Result**, **Approve Result**, **Raise Dispute / Request Exception**, **Correct Result**, and **Reset to Draft**.\n\nClub portal:\n\n```text\nMy Account > Results\n```\n\n**Recovery:** Reset an incorrect in-progress result to draft.  {"content": "# Sports Federation Club Roles and Portal\n\nVersion: 19.0.4.1.0\nOwner: Federation Platform Team\nLast reviewed: 2026-08-23\nReview cadence: Every release\n\nRole-oriented self-service portal for club representatives, officials, and tournament operators.\n\n## Primary user journeys\n\n### Club representative\n\n- manage club teams and players\n- submit season and tournament registrations\n- prepare and activate rosters\n- complete match sheets and readiness tasks\n- nominate officials\n- review result actions and deadlines\n\n### Official\n\n- view assignments\n- confirm or decline within the authorized scope\n- access relevant match information\n\n### Tournament operator\n\n- use the tournament operations board\n- monitor courts, matches, readiness, and action queues\n- execute scoped result and operational actions\n\n## Trust boundary\n\nAll privileged portal writes must use a model-owned method and the shared `federation.portal.privilege` boundary. Controllers validate input and resolve scope but do not perform raw elevated business writes. See `adr/0001-portal-trust-boundaries.md`.\n\nEvery new privileged route requires:\n\n1. positive in-scope coverage\n2. negative out-of-scope coverage\n3. direct-ID or guessed-record coverage\n4. model/helper ownership assertions when elevation is used\n5. CSRF enforcement for state-changing browser or JSON-RPC routes\n\n## Portal UX direction\n\nThe landing page should remain task-first. Common tasks are teams, registrations, upcoming matches, and action items. Specialist tools should be progressively disclosed instead of presented as an undifferentiated module catalogue.\n\n## Operations board\n\nThe board loads through scoped JSON-RPC, supports polling and structured failures, and exposes only matches and actions available to the current user. Server-side checks remain authoritative.\n\n## Tests\n\nThe module includes HTTP smoke, ownership, access-denied, team, player, roster, registration, officiating, result, accessibility, mobile, operations-board, and end-to-end portal workflow tests.\n\n## Consolidated documentation\n\n`PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_COVERAGE.md`, `PORTAL_OWNERSHIP_TEST_MATRIX.md`, and `ROADMAP_RC.md` are deleted. Their durable rules are consolidated here and in ADR-0001; the test files are the authoritative live coverage map.\n\n## competition portal\n\nThe active competition portal is edition-based. Participation comes from\ncompetition entries and finalized participant sets. Match-day schedule data is\nrendered only from each match day's current live publication. Draft schedules,\nreview evidence and superseded publications are intentionally unavailable.\n\nPrimary routes:\n\n- `/my/competitions`\n- `/my/competition-entries`\n- `/my/match-days`\n- `/sports/match-days/<id>/operations`\n\nLegacy tournament workspace routes are redirect-only and render no V1 data.\nThe backend tournament-registration action is loaded before the menus that use\nit, so a fresh module install and an upgrade both build the registration menu\nwithout relying on stale database metadata.\n\n\n## Accessible error recovery and focus management\n\nPortal forms move keyboard focus to server-rendered error summaries, connect\ninvalid controls to that summary with `aria-describedby`, and announce the\nsummary through an assertive live region. Bootstrap confirmation dialogs move\nfocus into the dialog and restore it to the invoking control when closed.\nKeyboard focus uses a visible outline that does not depend on color-only status\ncues. The focused accessibility suite covers these contracts together with\nmobile table and action wrapping.\n", "content_length": 3540, "filesystem_mode": "0644", "git_mode": "100644", "git_state": "tracked", "path": "sports_federation_portal/README.md", "record_type": "file", "sha256": "3ea4f6e8c7c0686f04a9a5a78e3b76b66861847771f9655441258519bd4016a5", "size_bytes": 3540}

scope.\n- ``group_id`` (Many2one): Optional group scope.\n- ``competition_id`` (Many2one): Competition context.\n- ``rule_set_id`` (Many2one): Scoring and tie-break rules.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``draft``, ``computed``, or ``frozen``.\n- ``line_ids`` (One2many): Ranked team entries.\n- ``line_count`` (Integer): Stat-button counter.\n- ``computed_on`` (Datetime): When the table was last computed.\n- ``notes`` (Text): Additional notes.\n\nState machine:\n\n- ``draft -> computed -> frozen``.\n\n``federation.standing.line``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nOne row per participant in the standings table.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Parent standings.\n- ``participant_id`` (Many2one): The team.\n- ``rank`` (Integer): Position in the standings table (1 = first).\n- ``played`` (Integer): Total matches played.\n- ``won`` / ``drawn`` / ``lost`` (Integer): Results breakdown.\n- ``score_for`` / ``score_against`` (Integer): Goals/points scored and conceded.\n- ``score_diff`` (Integer, computed): ``score_for - score_against``.\n- ``points`` (Integer): Total points per rule set.\n- ``note`` (Char): Short free-text remark for this line.\n- ``tiebreak_notes`` (Text, readonly): Auto-generated explanation of the tie-break criterion used to order this participant.\n\n``federation.standing.recompute.job``\n~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~\n\nAsynchronous recompute queue record used for background standings updates.\n\nFields:\n\n- ``standing_id`` (Many2one): Target standing to recompute.\n- ``idempotency_key`` (Char): Replay-safe key for deduplicating repeated queue requests.\n- ``correlation_id`` (Char): Trace identifier propagated through queue processing.\n- ``state`` (Selection): ``pending``, ``running``, ``done``, or ``failed``.\n- ``attempt_count`` / ``max_attempts`` (Integer): Retry control metadata.\n- ``requested_on`` / ``started_on`` / ``completed_on`` (Datetime): Lifecycle timestamps.\n- ``next_retry_on`` (Datetime): Retry schedule for failed jobs.\n- ``last_error`` (Text): Last failure reason captured for operators.\n\nKey Behaviours\n--------------\n\n- **Rule-set driven scoring**: points are calculated using the +#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Validate the product-facing release-candidate qualification contracts."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import ast
+import csv
+import json
+import sys
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+
+
+def load_json(relative):
+    return json.loads((ROOT / relative).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
+
+
+def acl_rows():
+    rows = []
+    for path in ROOT.glob("sports_federation_*/security/ir.model.access.csv"):
+        with path.open(encoding="utf-8", newline="") as handle:
+            rows.extend(
+                dict(row, _path=str(path.relative_to(ROOT)))
+                for row in csv.DictReader(handle)
+            )
+    return rows
+
+
+def main():
+    errors = []
+    role_matrix = load_json("ci/rc_role_matrix.json")
+    recovery = load_json("ci/rc_recovery_contract.json")
+    profiles = load_json("ci/rc_performance_profiles.json")
+    if (
+        role_matrix.get("schema_version") != 1
+        or recovery.get("schema_version") != 1
+        or profiles.get("schema_version") != 1
+    ):
+        errors.append("all RC contracts must use schema_version 1")
+
+    rows = acl_rows()
+    for group, contract in role_matrix["roles"].items():
+        group_rows = [row for row in rows if row.get("group_id:id") == group]
+        for model in contract.get("can_read", []):
+            model_ref = "model_" + model.replace(".", "_")
+            if not any(
+                row.get("model_id:id", "").split(".")[-1] == model_ref
+                and row.get("perm_read") == "1"
+                for row in group_rows
+            ):
+                errors.append(f"{group} lacks declared read access to {model}")
+        for key, permission in (
+            ("must_not_write", "perm_write"),
+            ("must_not_create", "perm_create"),
+        ):
+            for model in contract.get(key, []):
+                model_ref = "model_" + model.replace(".", "_")
+                if any(
+                    row.get("model_id:id", "").split(".")[-1] == model_ref
+                    and row.get(permission) == "1"
+                    for row in group_rows
+                ):
+                    errors.append(f"{group} unexpectedly has {permission} on {model}")
+
+    for name, contract in recovery["workflows"].items():
+        path = ROOT / contract["source"]
+        if not path.is_file():
+            errors.append(f"{name}: missing source {contract['source']}")
+            continue
+        tree = ast.parse(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), filename=str(path))
+        methods = {
+            node.name
+            for node in ast.walk(tree)
+            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef))
+        }
+        for action in contract["actions"]:
+            if action not in methods:
+                errors.append(f"{name}: missing recovery action {action}")
+
+    expected_profiles = {"small", "medium", "large"}
+    if set(profiles.get("profiles", {})) != expected_profiles:
+        errors.append("performance profiles must define small, medium, and large")
+    previous = 0
+    for name in ("small", "medium", "large"):
+        clubs = profiles.get("profiles", {}).get(name, {}).get("clubs", 0)
+        if not isinstance(clubs, int) or clubs <= previous:
+            errors.append("performance profile club counts must increase")
+        previous = clubs
+
+    required = (
+        "sports_federation_demo/tests/test_operator_role_acceptance.py",
+        "sports_federation_demo/tests/test_browser_competition_lifecycle.py",
+        "sports_federation_demo/tests/test_demo_data_pack.py",
+        "docs/RELEASE_PILOT_SCENARIO.md",
+        "scripts/ci/run_release_baseline.sh",
+        "scripts/ci/run_migration_rehearsal.sh",
+    )
+    for relative in required:
+        if not (ROOT / relative).is_file():
+            errors.append(f"missing RC evidence surface: {relative}")
+
+    if errors:
+        print("RC product readiness failed:", file=sys.stderr)
+        for error in errors:
+            print(f"- {error}", file=sys.stderr)
+        return 1
+    print("RC product readiness contracts passed.")
+    return 0
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    raise SystemExit(main())
+
